assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Dropping fixture pointers or reading the wrong isolated home makes the 240-pointer assertion fail.
An incomplete exhaustive claim read fails the 240 distinct run IDs check; the expected count is independently fixed by three repositories times 80 pointers.
An exhaustive reader that leaves any disposition unread fails the all-read assertion.
A narrowed read losing or adding any admission, conflict, warning or validation verdict fails equality against the separately obtained exhaustive claim population.
Skipping the measured claim read or repeating it fails the exactly-one-measurement assertion.
A broken git-call instrument observing no identity probe fails the nonempty calls assertion.
Restoring the base unfiltered call causes 243 git subprocesses and fails the independent ceiling of 20; the recorded negative control demonstrates this for both parameters.
A claim read exceeding six seconds fails the independent elapsed-time ceiling.
Changing the narrowed figure verdict relative to the independently read exhaustive population fails full verdict equality.
Silently admitting an exclusive collision or returning a different refusal type fails the literal refused state and scope-conflict assertions.
Attributing the collision to a different run fails comparison to the known first alpha pointer; this checks identity, not a caller-supplied expected verdict.

Reporting the wrong candidate path or omitting the refusal fails the known figure-path assertion; although the path originates in fixture input, the result is derived by conflict resolution and does not move automatically with it.
Retaining a removed claim or refusing a disjoint repository after unlinking the alpha holder fails the independently specified admitted verdict.
Filtering by the primary repository alone admits an absolute foreign figure path or names the wrong owner, failing the refused state or literal r-beta-000 identity.
